EEI Corp Unveils Modular Construction Solution, Eyes Efficiency Gains in Philippine Market

EEI Corp, a leading player in the Philippine engineering and construction sector, has announced the launch of its new modular construction solution, aiming to streamline building processes and respond to growing demand for faster project delivery in the country.

The product, branded as EEI ModularBuild, was officially introduced at a press briefing held Thursday in Makati City. EEI Corp executives highlighted the system’s potential to reduce on-site construction time by up to 30% compared to conventional methods, a statistic that industry observers say could significantly improve project turnaround in the nation’s rapidly expanding urban centers.

“We are excited to present EEI ModularBuild as our answer to the evolving needs of developers and contractors,” said EEI Corp President Roberto Sison. “Our solution leverages precision manufacturing and advanced logistics to deliver high-quality modules that can be quickly assembled on site, minimizing disruptions and accelerating completion.”

Modular construction has gained traction globally in recent years, with proponents citing benefits such as improved quality control, labor efficiency, and reduced environmental impact. According to the Philippine Constructors Association, the local market is beginning to embrace prefabricated and modular technologies, particularly for mid- to high-rise residential and commercial developments.

“ModularBuild positions EEI Corp to capitalize on this trend,” remarked Maria Santos, a construction sector analyst at Manila-based brokerage firm Solido Capital. “The Philippine construction industry is under pressure to deliver more projects in less time, given the government’s infrastructure push and private sector investments. Solutions that can deliver speed without compromising standards are in high demand.”

Company officials noted that EEI ModularBuild is initially targeting projects in Metro Manila and Cebu, with plans to expand its reach through partnerships with local developers. The system is designed to accommodate a range of building types, from schools to offices and residential towers.

“We have already received inquiries from several developers interested in piloting ModularBuild for their upcoming projects,” added Sison. “Our aim is to support the country’s growth by making construction more efficient and sustainable.”

Shares of EEI Corp closed flat at PHP 4.85 on Thursday, in line with the broader market. Investors and industry stakeholders will be watching early project results closely as the company seeks to carve out a larger footprint in the modular construction segment.
